The Pension Operators Association of Nigeria (PenOp) has clarified that the N52,500 Minimum Pension Guarantee unveiled by the National Pension Commission (PenCom) applies only to eligible Federal Government retirees under the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS). Head of Media, Brands and Communications at PenOp, Mrs Adeola Oyegbade, made the clarification at the association’s 2026 Annual Media Retreat, held virtually on Tuesday. The retreat was themed “Telling the Pension Story: The Journey So Far”. Oyegbade emphasised that the initiative did not cover all public and private sector retirees. She explained that eligible beneficiaries would receive the minimum pension automatically, subject to applicable conditions, without having to apply separately. Clarifying further on programmed withdrawal, Oyegbade explained that retirees’ monthly payments were determined using an actuarial table and the amounts accumulated in their Retirement Savings Accounts (RSAs). She said private sector retirees would continue to receive benefits based on the amounts accumulated in their RSAs. She advised workers to make additional voluntary contributions (AVCs) or invest in other financial instruments to improve their income after retirement. According to her, the statutory contributions by employers and employees might not be sufficient to sustain the standard of living workers enjoyed during active service. “Your pension is for when you retire, but the kind of life you want to live after retirement requires additional planning,” she said. Tinubu had recently launched the N52,500 monthly minimum pension guarantee. 173,209 retirees were identified as eligible beneficiaries. https://punchng.com/tinubu-launches-n52500-minimum-pension-for-173209-retirees/ Meanwhile, also speaking on Tuesday, Mrs Anthonia Ifeanyi-Okoro, Chief Executive Officer of PenOp, said pension operators were intensifying efforts to expand coverage among informal sector workers. She said this would be achieved through the Personal Pension Plan, in collaboration with PenCom, trade associations and technology partners. She noted that the initiative would include engagements with market associations, domestic workers, drivers and other informal sector groups to encourage pension participation. On data recapture, Ifeanyi-Okoro said Pension Fund Administrators had organised roadshows, webinars and physical engagements with employers to encourage contributors to update their records. She attributed the slow response partly to the absence of penalties for delays and urged Retirement Savings Account holders to complete the exercise to facilitate access to their pension benefits. (NAN) Agency Report
